A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SplatFormer study. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable, and retained content can be matched across reordering and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original quantitative and qualitative experiments on synthetic objects, real-world captures and MVImgNet, together with architecture and supervision ablations.

after.justification: v3 retains original experiments and adds geometry measurements, camera-condition tests, inference measurements and an EscherNet comparison.

M1.justification: Appendix B revises the stated upsampling arrangement: grid-pooling precedes every up-pooling stage except the first in v1, versus except the last in v3. This is a limited architectural specification change; the PDFs do not establish whether implementation changed. The PTv3 backbone, residual refinement and L1-plus-LPIPS objective remain.

E1.justification: The datasets remain ShapeNet, Objaverse, GSO, iPhone captures and MVImgNet. Within this coverage, v3 adds close-up GSO views, reversed high-elevation-input/low-elevation-test conditions on Objaverse, and explicit depth/normal evaluation. These extend existing tasks and scenarios without introducing a new data domain.

E2.justification: Table 1 and appendix comparisons add EscherNet, evaluated using all 32 input views at inference. The InstantSplat comparison changes from a DUSt3R-initialized 3DGS proxy in v1 Appendix D to the official InstantSplat implementation in v3 Appendix G. Other comparator membership is retained.

E3.justification: Appendix A changes test azimuth sampling from random to uniformly strided, and Appendix B changes Objaverse spherical-harmonic degree from 3 to 1. InstantSplat replaces random point subsampling and the standard 3DGS optimization recipe with overlap/confidence filtering and 3,000 iterations. New experiments introduce depth/normal MAE, camera-radius sweeps and reversed-view testing. These are substantial reported protocol changes; they do not establish that every retained result was rerun.

E4.justification: v3 adds geometry-fidelity analysis (Appendix D), joint camera-radius/elevation robustness tests (E), a zero-shot reversed-view failure test (H), and inference-capacity testing through additional noisy Gaussians (B). These substantially broaden the questions examined. The backbone, residual-prediction, denoising and 2D-versus-3D supervision analyses already existed in v1.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. Averaging over scenes and camera configurations remains; the new result tables do not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Table 1 replaces InstantSplat and SyncDreamer results under revised implementations/documentation: ShapeNet PSNR changes from 19.00 to 18.49 and 9.07 to 17.26, respectively. EscherNet and substantial geometry, camera-sweep and efficiency results are added. Table H.1 reports limited reversed-view improvement, 18.22 versus 18.01 PSNR. Table E.1 includes two 20-degree settings favoring 3DGS. SplatFormer's original principal benchmark scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The Gaussian rendering equations, residual-refinement formulation and loss definitions remain unchanged. Neither version contains added theorems or proofs. The new geometry measurements are evaluation procedures, not new mathematical theory.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets and conclusion retain the same central claims: introduce OOD-NVS evaluation, refine Gaussian splats with a point transformer, and improve rendering under the studied OOD conditions. Added experiments support or qualify these claims without redefining the main contribution.

C2.justification: v1 treats more diverse camera setups mainly as future work. v3 explicitly explains weak high-to-low transfer through unobserved geometry and unfamiliar artifact distributions, and proposes broader training or generative capabilities. It also discusses spatial-distribution-dependent memory consumption and distinguishes rendering improvement from surface extraction. Existing texture, real-world and unbounded-scene limitations remain.

D1.justification: v3 newly documents the 100k-Gaussian training cap, 10k-step test initialization, inference time and memory, and detailed EscherNet and revised baseline recipes. Reported training hardware changes from RTX 3090 to RTX 4090. Section 4.1 changes a promised data/rendering-code release to a statement that these resources have been released. Together these substantially expand reproducibility information.

R1.justification: v3 adds references including EscherNet, GaussianObject, 3DGS-Enhancer, LSM and CVT-xRF. Related work now explicitly discusses LSM's point-transformer-based Gaussian prediction and CVT-xRF's transformer-based reconstruction. The positioning around refining existing Gaussian splats remains, so this is a focused update rather than a wholesale reframing.

P1.justification: The introduction, related work and experimental setup receive localized rewriting. The appendix moves baseline implementations after comparisons and introduces separate geometry and diverse-view sections. Conference headers and expanded acknowledgements are added, while most exposition and the main section structure remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds Tables D.1, E.1 and H.1 and the geometry visualization in Figure H.3. Comparison tables and qualitative grids accommodate EscherNet, and the MVImgNet figure replaces two examples with four in a revised arrangement. Main Figures 1–5 and most existing displays retain their content and design.

improvement.justification: v3 provides better support and clearer boundaries for the existing contribution through the all-input EscherNet comparison, official InstantSplat implementation, geometry/close-up tests and explicit reversed-view failure analysis. Added implementation details and reported resource release improve reproducibility. The gain is limited by remaining reporting inconsistencies, including the three-day SyncDreamer budget described as matching SplatFormer despite Appendix B reporting approximately two days for SplatFormer training.
